02 / THE MECHANICSSMALL CHECKS, BIG RELIEF

The simplest part of your day, made clearer.

Slacker is a lightweight Chrome extension. No new inbox. No new way to work. Just useful signals inside Slack Web.

✓✓
01

Install Slacker

Add the Chrome extension and open Slack Web. It works quietly in the background.

↘
02

Send your message

A single check appears when your message is sent and tracked.

↗
03

See when it’s opened

When another Slacker user opens the conversation, your indicator turns to two teal checks. Hover to see the time.

✓✓
03 / THE HONEST PARTTHE TWO-PERSON RULE

A clearer signal.
On both sides.

Seen works when both people have Slacker. It means the other person opened the conversation with your message in view. It isn’t an official Slack read receipt or a promise that they’ve replied.

05 / PRIVACY, SIMPLY

The receipt matters.
Your message stays yours.

Slacker uses temporary Slack message identifiers and seen timestamps to provide receipts. Full message content is not uploaded to the Slacker server. Local settings and receipt history remain in your browser.

Read our Privacy Policy ↗
06 / GOOD TO KNOWFREQUENTLY ASKED

Questions? Fair.

Clarity should come with clear answers.

Does Slacker work with everyone on Slack?

Seen status works when both people have Slacker installed and are using Slack Web in Chrome.

Does Slacker read my messages?

Slacker detects message activity in Slack Web to display receipts, but full message text is not uploaded to the Slacker server.

Do I need to create an account?

No. Slacker does not require a separate account.

Can I turn it off?

Yes. You can disable Slacker from the extension popup at any time.

Is Slacker free?

Yes, Slacker is currently free to use.

07 / YOUR TURN

Stop wondering whether your message was seen.

Try the current Chrome extension preview with a teammate. Both of you need Slacker for seen checks to appear.

Download Slacker for Chrome ↓
  1. Download and unzip the preview build.
  2. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
  3. Choose Load unpacked and select the unzipped folder.
  4. Ask a teammate to do the same, then open Slack in Chrome.
